pairs.subject: cost-metering
pairs.evidence: lib/spend/meter.ts:249 A call that reached a vendor but carries no positive figure bumps the `unpriced` counter and writes no row, so its model, outcome and attribution axes are lost; on the file store, rows are also pruned out of the state once the rolling window passes, so the meter is a ceiling window rather than a durable ledger.

techniques.evidence: lib/spend/meter.ts:343 The ceiling check and the hold run in one transaction, counting spent + held, so concurrent calls cannot all pass against the same total; 0 means spend nothing and an unset ceiling gets a bounded default (classes.ts header).
lib/spend/meter.ts:400 Reserve returns a hold; settle replaces it, and if a row cannot be read the hold is still released; release of an already-settled hold does nothing.

lib/spend/meter.ts:249 Failed calls are booked as rows (line 256), but an unpriced call becomes a counter instead of a row, and prune drops window-expired rows, so per-call history is not kept on transactional terms.
lib/spend/classes.ts:62 Each class declares its axes and an attribution axis; byAxis reports the spend that lacks it as `unattributed`.
lib/spend/meter.ts:446 stats() returns the window boundary together with the total, plus refusal, failed, unpriced, evicted and late-write counters.
packages/kernel/src/spend-requests/schema.ts:100 A spend request carries its estimate as a structure (lines, range, unpriced count, figure source), not a bare scalar.

pairs.subject: cost-metering
pairs.evidence: lib/imaging/router.ts:300 Recognize calls are billed per token and their price-table rows are deliberately unpriced, so every recognize call books $0 into the imaging ceiling (only the unpriced counter moves) instead of a declared conservative default; budget.ts:375 also reserves 0 when no per-image rate is declared at all.

techniques.evidence: lib/imaging/router.ts:312 A single router chokepoint reserves before any vendor is called, and takes a fresh reserve for each later candidate after a billed failure (line 391).
lib/imaging/router.ts:328 The hold is released in `finally` on every exit that did not settle it.
lib/imaging/router.ts:465 A billed failure is settled as an `outcome: failed` row with an estimate basis and a price ref.
lib/imaging/router.ts:300 Rows are versioned (priceRef provider/model@checked) and vendor figures win, but a known-unpriced class costs zero in the ledger rather than a declared default.
lib/imaging/pricing.ts:374 The estimate is the dearest declared per-image rate, with that assumption written into its note, and it hard-gates the call.
lib/imaging/budget.ts:233 Rows carry capability, the provider that actually served, the model, and the price row used.
lib/imaging/budget.ts:320 budgetStats returns the window boundary with the total and the counters; budgetForecast projects affordability and when spend can resume.

pairs.subject: cost-metering
pairs.evidence: lib/ledger/v1/sources/spend.ts:42 The ledger receives spend.book rows only if they are still inside the v1 window when it syncs, so per-call rows (with their attribution) can be missing, and the tally checks v1's own booked/evicted identity rather than counting rows the ledger missed.

techniques.evidence: lib/ledger/v1/sources/spend.ts:42 The cumulative counters fact keeps amounts reconcilable, but missed rows are a gap the ledger does not count.
lib/ledger/v1/sources/spend.ts:203 Any class whose rows and evictions do not add up is named as `unaccounted`.
lib/ledger/v1/sources/spend.ts:188 Class, unit, outcome, basis and every axis are carried onto the event.
lib/ledger/v1/sources/spend.ts:176 The projected cost keeps whether it is the vendor's figure (real) or a table estimate (model).
lib/ledger/v1/sources/spend.ts:29 These sources are read-only projections and start no metered spend.

pairs.subject: cost-metering
pairs.evidence: lib/decision/v1/sources/spend.ts:138 The packet meta adds every unpriced request as $0 and shows no unpriced share, so a pile of unpriced asks reads as a measured small total, which contradicts totalWords' own rule that unpriced is never $0.

techniques.evidence: lib/decision/v1/sources/spend.ts:138 The aggregate total drops the unpriced or default-priced share instead of marking it.
lib/decision/v1/sources/spend.ts:164 An agent's keep is refused, so only the operator can authorize spend.
lib/decision/v1/sources/spend.ts:186 The receipt is re-priced live, and its worst case becomes the launch's stop point; a price that changes between preview and commit refuses the commit.
lib/decision/v1/sources/spendWords.ts:77 Each request names the stable actor kind and id that asked.
